docs.summary:
A prefab asset: a serialized GameObject hierarchy, stored as raw EchoObject data. Holding a prefab keeps every asset its hierarchy uses loaded, so spawning it never loads.

Instantiating one lives on [`GameObject`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.GameObject) - see [`Instantiate`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.GameObject~Instantiate) to spawn into a scene, or [`InstantiateDetached`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.GameObject~InstantiateDetached) for the hierarchy on its own - so that every way of building a GameObject from serialized data goes through one place.
Where this prefab's contents come from. Set by whatever produces the asset.
True when this prefab is generated rather than authored, so nothing may be written back to it.

The serialized GameObject hierarchy in Echo format. Assigning takes a copy: every instantiation reads this tree, so a caller that kept a handle to what it assigned could otherwise change what future instances come out as.
Every asset the stored hierarchy names, loaded or not.
